summary: Multipath callback fanout causing asymmetric 429s and burst-pool contention — request for config recommendations
description:
Issue summary: BrightCart reports recurrent 429 responses for their callback-heavy ingestion pipeline after they rotated signed cookies and increased parallel callback workers. This affects real-time order enrichment and causes delayed deliveries to downstream systems.

Impact: Intermittent 429s (10-30% of callback requests rejected) across two regions during peak load windows, customer-facing latency increases of 2-6s due to retries, and duplicate retries causing increased downstream load. Customer is on Dedicated tier and worried about throughput guarantees.

Timeline: Customer rotated signed cookies at 2026-03-11T22:10Z and immediately scaled callback fanout from 8->40 parallel workers at 23:00Z. 429 wave began ~23:05Z and persisted in wave pattern until mitigation on 2026-03-12 by customer.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use signed-cookie based callback endpoints with short TTLs (30s).
2) Launch 40 parallel worker processes making callback POSTs every ~300ms after receiving an event.
3) Rapidly rotate signed cookies for session refresh every 20s.
4) Observe 5xx/429 spikes and asymmetric rejection (one NAT pool more affected).

Observed behavior: 429s surface primarily on callback route paths and during cookie refresh windows. Rate headers from gateway show token-window exhaustion early in refill interval. Some requests counted twice at edge due to connection re-establishment with new cookie.

Expected behavior: Signed-cookie rotation and callback fanout should not produce systemic tenant-level 429s if tenant has dedicated burst pool capacity. Customer expected per-route separation between low-latency callbacks and bulk retries.

Logs/Telemetry snippets: Provided by customer: truncated request_id list and Gateway rate headers: "x-rate-limit-remaining: 0", "x-rate-limit-reset: 7s" and edge-proxy logs showing duplicated CONNECT sequences when cookie refresh occurs. Link to customer-provided pcap and webhooks log: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/brightcart-support/artifacts/887100-wave-logs.zip

Customer ask: Detailed recommendations for rate/burst configuration to avoid asymmetric 429s from callback fanout and signed-cookie rotation, plus short-term mitigation steps we can apply from our side (route isolation, temporary burst allocation).
comments: 2026-03-12 08:15 - Elena Martinez: Opened with initial customer report and provided sample logs and request_ids. Customer notes they saw sudden 429s only after rotating cookies and increasing workers.

2026-03-12 09:02 - Riley Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Asked for exact cookie TTL, sample headers, and whether workers share IPs. Requested access to callback route telemetry in our console. Assigned to SRE for deeper digging.

2026-03-12 11:30 - SRE (A. Patel): Initial triage: observed refill-window sawtooth on tenant token bucket; NAT pool reuse concentrated requests into a small set of source IPs causing window exhaustion. Correlates with signed-cookie rotate period. Investigating duplicate accounting on edge reconnect.

2026-03-13 14:20 - Riley Chen (Support): Sent recommended short-term mitigations to customer (stagger cookie refresh, reduce parallel workers, and enable route-specific burst pool). Customer staging-tested staggered refresh and reported immediate reduction in 429s.

2026-03-14 10:05 - BrightCart (Customer): Confirmed temporary mitigations helped. Asked for permanent config and whether we can automatically isolate callback route into separate burst pool on their Dedicated instance.

2026-03-14 13:40 - Riley Chen (Support): Noted follow-ups with Product (Dedicated orchestration) to determine feasibility and roadmap for route-level isolated burst pools. Preparing runbook update and console guide.
investigation_notes: Edge accounting: observed cases where preflight and POST following cookie refresh both increment token counter before connection reset completes.
Refill interval telemetry: tenant token bucket refills every 60s; heavy fanout concentrated inside 5-15s windows causing early exhaustion.
NAT/IP concentration: due to ephemeral worker placement, 70% of requests during waves came from three egress IPs, causing per-connection counting skew on some gateway shards.
Route tagging: callback paths currently use generic 'ingest' route weight; no explicit low-latency route config or dedicated burst allocation.

Hypothesis: signed-cookie rotation plus parallel short-TTL refreshes creates a synchronized fanout that defeats smoothing and bursts credits into narrow intervals, producing tenant-side 429s despite Dedicated capacity.
Relevant dashboards: Token-Refill Heatmap (link in console), Gateway edge logs: /dashboards/brightcart/token-refill-heatmap, Traces: /traces/887100-wave
workaround: Customer applied staggered cookie refresh (random jitter 5-10s) and reduced parallel workers from 40->12. Support applied temporary console flag to treat callback route as higher-priority (soft route weight bump) which lowered immediate 429s. These are temporary and not a permanent quiesce for the bookkeeping issue.
resolution_notes: Applied temporary route weight increase for /callbacks on BrightCart dedicated instance to reduce immediate rejects (2026-03-13 09:05).
Customer implemented jittered cookie refresh and reduced worker parallelism which eliminated the synchronized refill spikes in their staging tests.
SRE confirmed duplicate counting windows on edge-proxy when connections re-established with new cookie; PR to add idempotency dedupe at edge is proposed (see related_github_prs).

Permanent mitigation options: 1) Expose console toggle to create isolated burst pools per-route for Dedicated tenants, 2) Implement edge-level preflight dedupe for rapid cookie rotation, 3) Add explicit guidance in Runbook for signed-cookie refresh patterns and worker jittering.
Owner for runbook update: Riley Chen. Owner for product change request: SRE lead (A. Patel).
next_steps: Create support runbook section for signed-cookie rotation best practices and publish to Confluence (owner: Riley Chen).
Product to evaluate feasibility and cost of console-exposed per-route burst pool for Dedicated customers (owner: Product Infra).
SRE to land PR for edge dedupe logic and coordinate a canary deployment (owner: A. Patel, related PR linked).
Schedule 30-minute post-mortem with BrightCart next week to review long-term plan and SLA implications.
Monitor tenant token-bucket metrics for next 72 hours and report back to customer with trend charts.
